Based on my search, I can provide you with comprehensive information about methane bonding.

## Methane Bond Structure

### Basic Molecular Structure
Methane (CH₄) is the simplest hydrocarbon, consisting of **one central carbon atom bonded to four hydrogen atoms**. The molecule has a **tetrahedral geometry** with the carbon atom at the center and the four hydrogen atoms positioned at the vertices of a regular tetrahedron.

### Bond Characteristics

| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| Bond type | C-H single bonds (sigma bonds) |
| Number of bonds | 4 |
| Bond angle (H-C-H) | 109.5° |
| Bond length | ~109.7 pm (picometers) |
| Molecular geometry | Tetrahedral |
| Hybridization | sp³ |

### Hybridization and Bond Formation

The carbon atom in methane undergoes **sp³ hybridization**:

1. **Ground state**: Carbon's electron configuration is 1s² 2s² 2p²
2. **Excited state**: One 2s electron is promoted to the empty 2p orbital, giving four unpaired electrons
3. **Hybridization**: One 2s orbital and three 2p orbitals mix to form **four equivalent sp³ hybrid orbitals**
4. **Bond formation**: Each sp³ orbital overlaps with a hydrogen 1s orbital to form a **sigma (σ) bond**

All four C-H bonds are **equivalent and nonpolar** due to the symmetrical tetrahedral arrangement. Although there is a small electronegativity difference between carbon (2.55) and hydrogen (2.20), the molecule is **nonpolar overall** because the bond dipoles cancel out in the symmetrical tetrahedral geometry.

### Bonding Theory Explanation

According to **VSEPR theory** (Valence Shell Electron Pair Repulsion), the four bonding electron pairs around the central carbon atom arrange themselves to minimize repulsion, resulting in the tetrahedral shape with 109.5° bond angles. This is the maximum possible separation for four electron pairs around a central atom.

1. https://www.britannica.com/science/methane
2. https://www.chemtube3d.com/vseprshapech4/
3. https://www.guidechem.com/guideview/lab/what-is-the-lewis-structure-of-methane-ch4.html
4. https://biocheminsider.com/molecular-geometry-of-methane/
5. https://kunduz.com/en/blog/ch4-methane-lewis-structure-294663/
